title: Hamburg and the band staying the same until Russia
summary: After Berlin they play the Thalia Theater in Hamburg; George Howe leaves for home before Russia.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Where did you then go, from Berlin?
We went to Hamburg, the Thalia Theater in Hamburg. And we stayed there about two or three weeks, I think. Because -- we could have stayed longer. Not because the
crowd had died down, but we had to go over to Sweden.
You had commitments. Did the same reception in Hamburg greeted you that --
Same as -- from then on, our receptions were -- up into Russia, they were all the same.
Because, we being the first, some things was greater than others. But we were in that thing -- we had no trouble at all.
Was anybody beginning to get homesick? There were some changes in the show, weren't there, in personnel?
Some changes in the show, but not in the band.

The band stayed the same up until Russia. Going into Russia, George Howard decided that he didn't -- he wanted to go home. It wasn't George as much as it was his chorus girlfriend. She wanted to go and George thought, 'Well, I'll go home.' And he regretted it many a day, before he died. He regretted that. But he left on account of that and we replaced him.
